items.finding: The registry accepts arbitrary HTTPS destinations and the worker resolves them at send time without restricting private or infrastructure address ranges, allowing a partner-controlled URL to reach internal services or metadata endpoints.
The HMAC covers only the body and the request has no freshness input, so anyone who captures a valid request can replay it for as long as the event remains useful.
A single environment secret authenticates every partner connection, so compromise of one partner credential permits forged requests to all partners and makes revocation non-selective.
The profile sends customer contact and shipping fields even though the approved standard profile and data policy exclude those personal-data fields, creating unauthorized disclosure to partners.

Changing the signing secret requires restarting the worker deployment and cannot select old and new keys during an overlap, leaving rotation dependent on a coordinated interruption and risking failed deliveries.
All tenants share one FIFO delivery queue and worker claim path, so a slow or failing partner can consume retry capacity and violate the stated cross-tenant delay target for unrelated tenants.
The design retains complete request payloads in delivery records and logs for 365 days, conflicting with the 14-day default, 30-day maximum, and redacted-digest retention policy.
